    <us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock
      contextRef="C_1d47f543-1eb6-43b7-a011-30119db2d03c"
      id="F_18c7a543-b352-4330-b85b-805750062790">&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;8.   &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;SLB&#x2019;s functional currency is primarily the US dollar. However, outside the United States, a significant portion of SLB&#x2019;s expenses is incurred in foreign currencies. Therefore, when the US dollar weakens (strengthens) in relation to the foreign currencies of the countries in which SLB conducts business, the US dollar-reported expenses will increase (decrease).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Changes in foreign currency exchange rates expose SLB to risks on future cash flows relating to its fixed rate debt denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. SLB uses cross-currency interest rate swaps to provide a hedge against these risks. These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges, with the fair value of the derivative recorded on the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;and in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Accumulated other comprehensive loss. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Amounts recorded in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; Accumulated other comprehensive loss &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;are reclassified into earnings in the same period or periods that the hedged item is recognized in earnings.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Details regarding SLB&#x2019;s outstanding cross-currency interest rate swaps as of September 30, 2024, were as follows:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;display:flex;margin-top:6pt;justify-content:flex-start;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:0;min-width:4.537%;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;min-width:4.7521786492374725%;word-break:keep-all;display:inline-flex;justify-content:flex-start;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div style="width:100%;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;During 2019, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of SLB issued &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of Euro-denominated debt. SLB entered into cross-currency interest rate swaps in order to hedge changes in the US dollar value of its &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.00&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Notes due 2024, &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.25&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.50&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Notes due 2031. These cross-currency interest rate swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.29&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;%, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.51&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.76&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;%, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;display:flex;margin-top:0;justify-content:flex-start;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:0;min-width:4.537%;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;min-width:4.7521786492374725%;word-break:keep-all;display:inline-flex;justify-content:flex-start;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div style="width:100%;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;During 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of SLB issued &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of Euro-denominated debt. SLB entered into cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge changes in the US dollar value of its &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.25&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Notes due 2027 and &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.50&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Notes due 2031. These cross-currency interest rate swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.87&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.20&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;%, respectively. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;display:flex;margin-top:0;justify-content:flex-start;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:0;min-width:4.537%;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;min-width:4.7521786492374725%;word-break:keep-all;display:inline-flex;justify-content:flex-start;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div style="width:100%;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;During 2020, a US-dollar functional currency subsidiary of SLB issued &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of Euro-denominated debt. SLB entered into cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge changes in the US dollar value of its &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.375&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Guaranteed Notes due 2026 and &#x20ac;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.00&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Guaranteed Notes due 2032. These cross-currency interest rate swaps effectively convert the Euro-denominated notes to US-dollar denominated debt with fixed annual interest rates of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;2.77&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;3.49&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;%, respectively. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class="item-list-element-wrapper" style="margin-left:4.528%;display:flex;margin-top:0;justify-content:flex-start;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:0;min-width:4.537%;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Times New Roman;min-width:4.7521786492374725%;word-break:keep-all;display:inline-flex;justify-content:flex-start;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;div style="width:100%;display:inline;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;During 2020, a Canadian dollar functional currency subsidiary of SLB issued $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion of US dollar denominated debt. SLB entered into cross-currency interest rate swaps to hedge changes in the US dollar value of its $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;0.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.40&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;% Senior Notes due 2025. These cross-currency interest rate swaps effectively convert the US dollar notes to Canadian dollar denominated debt with a fixed annual interest rate of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;1.73&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;%.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;A summary of the amounts included in the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; Consolidated Balance Sheet&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; relating to cross currency interest rate swaps was as follows:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

      &lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;The fair values were determined using a model with inputs that are observable in the market or can be derived or corroborated by observable data.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:left;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;SLB is exposed to risks on future cash flows to the extent that the local currency is not the functional currency and expenses denominated in local currency are not equal to revenues denominated in local currency. SLB uses foreign currency forward contracts to provide a hedge against a portion of these cash flow risks. These contracts are accounted for as cash flow hedges.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;SLB is also exposed to changes in the fair value of assets and liabilities denominated in currencies other than the functional currency. While SLB uses foreign currency forward contracts to economically hedge this exposure as it relates to certain currencies, these contracts are not designated as hedges for accounting purposes. Instead, the fair value of the derivative is recorded on the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Consolidated Balance Sheet &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;and changes in the fair value are recognized in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;as are changes in the fair value of the hedged item.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Foreign currency forward contracts were outstanding for the US dollar equivalent of $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;7.1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion and $&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;5.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; billion in various foreign currencies as of September 30, 2024 and December 31, 2023, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Other than the previously mentioned cross-currency interest rate swaps, the fair value of the other outstanding derivatives &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;t material &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;as of September 30, 2024 and December 31, 2023.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;div style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Arial;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0;font-family:Times New Roman;margin-bottom:0;text-align:justify;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;The effect of derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges, and those not designated as hedges, on the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;font-style:italic;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;Consolidated Statement of Income &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt;was as follows:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;white-space:pre-wrap;font-size:9pt;font-family:Arial;min-width:fit-content;"&gt; A liability is accrued when a loss is both probable and can be reasonably estimated. Management believes that the probability of a material loss with respect to any currently pending legal proceeding is remote. However, litigation is inherently uncertain, and it is not possible to predict the ultimate disposition of any of these proceedings. &lt;/span&gt;</us-gaap:LossContingencyDisclosures>
